occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred labourer's household (2 of 12 this layer infers): hh_inf_labourer_south_02 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.name: An inferred labourer's household (south division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_d1_033 is an anonymous inferred roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.
residents.basis: An anonymous roof of the reconstruction programme, ADOPTED by this household rather than raised for it. The roof's own existence and position stay conjectural; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit.

persons.name: A labourer (inferred resident, unnamed)
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. The name field carries a designation because inventing a surname would make this record indistinguishable at a glance from the documented layer beside it. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE SECOND OF 12 LABOURER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER INFERS. THE LARGEST TRADE IN ANY WESTERN TOWN AND THE ONE NO ROSTER RECORDS, because a labourer advertises nothing, holds no office and joins no church committee - the three ways almost every documented person in this dataset became documented. The harbour works were under construction through 1834 and 1835 (both piers are structure records here), the streets were being graded, and several hundred buildings were being raised. Twelve labouring households are inferred - the largest single group in this layer and still a small fraction of what 3,265 people implies - and every one of them is housed in the meanest roof the schedule carries: a D1 log cabin or a D2 plank shanty.

residents.research_note: INFERRED HOUSEHOLD - second of 12 labourer households in this layer, in the south division. THE LARGEST TRADE IN ANY WESTERN TOWN AND THE ONE NO ROSTER RECORDS, because a labourer advertises nothing, holds no office and joins no church committee - the three ways almost every documented person in this dataset became documented. The harbour works were under construction through 1834 and 1835 (both piers are structure records here), the streets were being graded, and several hundred buildings were being raised. Twelve labouring households are inferred - the largest single group in this layer and still a small fraction of what 3,265 people implies - and every one of them is housed in the meanest roof the schedule carries: a D1 log cabin or a D2 plank shanty. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
